newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Harvey Norman sales up, sees more rises.
newsitem.headline: Harvey Norman sales up, sees more rises.

text.p: Household goods and electrical retailer Harvey Norman Ltd said on Tuesday its sales in the first four months of the 1996/97 year (July-June) rose 11.3 percent to A$361.9 million.
Harvey Norman chairman Gerry Harvey told the annual meeting the company expected sales to rise 15 to 16 percent in 1996/97 and that it saw strong sales in November and December.
"Sales for the four months is an increase of 11.3 percent on last year to A$361.9 million," Harvey said.
Harvey said the sales increase was less than the company's target of a 15 to 16 percent increase for the year to June 30.
"On that basis (of four months sales), it could be difficult to achieve, however, I don't think it will be a problem," he said.
"We're looking at a strong November and December and I think January and February will be pretty good as well," Harvey said.
